inputs.text: M.K. Stalin’s DMK manifesto is heavy on handouts: doubling women’s monthly aid to Rs 2,000, Rs 8,000 household coupons, and free motor pumpsets for farmers. These may be presented as help, but voters should ask how such promises will be paid for and whether they strengthen families and self-reliance—or make more people dependent on government. FDI, jobs and AI development sound more forward-looking, while support for fishermen matters too; still, a serious plan should put lasting work and economic responsibility ahead of ever-expanding giveaways.

output.main_topic: Criticism of the DMK manifesto’s handout-heavy promises and emphasis on lasting work and economic responsibility
subtopics: FDI, jobs, AI development, and support for fishermen
